comment: The negative variants that today's tools run, on the layered rendition (wave 013 run 0070, rewritten for the layers by wave 014: W-9 moved it to layered/, W-11 added V1 and V3 to V10; the cases of the plateaus of waves 008 to 013 went with the old mechanism, and N41 is the key itself). Each case is Brightcart's layered/ with the alteration `ops` (replace: the text must occur once or more, the first occurrence is replaced, or every one with `all`; write; copy; delete; paths are relative to the folder). Nothing negative is committed as a workspace: BrightcartNegativeCasesTest.java (command line) and brightcart-negative.test.js (editor) build each altered folder in a temporary folder from layered/ and check `cli` and `editor` below. `cli`: the arguments after `archicode -w <workspace>`, the exit code and the lines of the error output (the warnings and one `error:` line, and no stack trace); `sameStdoutAs`: another command whose standard output is the same. `editor`: the plateau the page draws (null: none is asked for) and what it compares it with (`@past`: the plateau it overrides), then what it shows: fatalError, treeProblems and treeWarnings (the tree of the plateaus), layerProblems (what the first layer of the chain that is wrong says), baselineProblem, manifestErrors (file -> text), danglingRelationships, duplicates, warnings (those of the comparison). The editor says the sentence of the command line up to three differences, which the node test removes before it compares: the banners start with a capital and end with a full stop, the plateau rules come under a heading (`Could not read the plateaus of workspace.yaml:`, `Could not read/parse workspace.yaml: `), and the position `(line L, column C)` of a file is not told. One cause is one sentence in both tools: while a manifest is refused the command line stops there, so the editor says that file and not what its absence leaves behind (N21, N22, N26, N28); the elements declared under a parent that is not there are one sentence with how many others there are (N45), and so are the elements that point at one reference that is not there (N47). An entry `editor: null` has a `reason`: the page has nothing to type.
